assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_HIKARU_AKUTSU_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (20,829 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Akutsu Hikaru (阿久津ヒカル) confined to the first story of Asaura's Japanese Gluttony days, 第一話『ファントム・メナス』 (spine items S9-S10), located by spine item and paragraph. assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Gluttony days, first story only. His history belongs to him at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: a friendship with Mika begun through work in Mika's wild-life years before DA and interrupted for ten years; a company founded in South America and business now mostly in the Middle East; a wife who died when Clarisse was little, the circumstances and his bereavement unrecounted; Mustangs kept serviced around the world; systema as exercise. Located present states, all within one day: arrival, the coffee joke and the Mustang with a carsick daughter (9.98-151); Chisato's guess about the name and the systema demonstration (9.152-198); the briefing, the defiance of the threat and Kurumi's challenge (9.210-243); departure (9.216-246); unreachable with his phone off, and no watcher of his (9.700-722, 10.323-340); hurrying back and asking for Clarisse (10.371-383); Kurumi's accusation, his reach, Mika's restraint and challenge, and his concession (10.373-625); Mika's appeal to trust and his departure making a call (10.598-615); the after-hours park and the false claim of advance preparation (10.933-951). Nothing after the story.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait's stated expectation is that he acts energetically on a problem as he understands it and tries to let the beneficiary see only a finished solution, supported by the maintained Mustang (9.98-115), the staged protection (9.283-304) and the after-hours park (10.933-951). It locates his defiance of a threat as a wish to be himself, 俺は俺らしくありたいのさ (9.210-243); the latitude he gives Mika (9.700-722, 10.598-615); and his blindness, under a stranger's accusation, to how his approach looks from the other side (10.575-598). It predicts his mistakes: treating a diagnosed cause as if it disposed of the danger (9.641-653), arranging a scene to produce a reaction, as his daughter also does, the false claim of advance preparation, and frightening someone with less power. Not B: the portrait calls his declaration of principle poor evidence that he would choose a contract over a daughter he believed was in danger, and says the evidence is much weaker for any claim that he will always choose business first. Work and daughter never conflict in this story because he arranged both, so the motive that would decide a real conflict is not established. That is insufficiency. Why he invents the lead time, to spare her or to spare himself, does not change the act and is productive uncertainty. Not D: one dedicated portrait states a located operational expectation and where it stops.

Located states within one day: delegation and departure, unreachability, return, confrontation, the reversal in which he must extend trust to the girls, and the evening he gives Clarisse. The portrait finds no new rule about his travel, no conversation with Clarisse about the hired pair and no permanent change to his priorities. Not C: there is no located change in him across time. Not E: the within-day states are located by paragraph.

Located written forms: no honorifics, a familiar opener and the bad-coffee joke with Mika (9.108-129); 娘を頼むよ entrusting his daughter; お嬢さん方 for the young women and お嬢ちゃん for Kurumi; 俺 clustering where someone would tell him how a man should act (9.217-243); the bare クラリスは？ (10.371-383); a counter-question about Mika's judgment of him, then asking what to do (10.584-613). Not B: one story, written register only, and the portrait says the novel offers no performed accent or vocal timing. Not D: several quoted forms differ by interlocutor.

Located tastes and habits: the Mustang kept in storage and serviced, and Mustangs waiting for him elsewhere (9.98-115); appraising Mika's coffee; systema as exercise (9.173-198); the Clarice Starling reference; ramen with Clarisse on other occasions, in her account; noticing her carsickness and letting her recover (9.130-139). Not B: his daily life in either region where he works, his education and his temperament with employees are unknown. Not D: several distinct habits and tastes are located.

Directed differences: Mika (ease without honorifics, trust whatever the request, accepting restraint and admonition, asking what to do, 9.108-129, 10.575-615); Clarisse (affection, a kiss and a departure she calls usual, a substitute day, the return and the park, without telling her when he understood, 9.216-246, 10.933-951); Chisato and Takina (credit for perception and skill, laughing from the floor, then having to extend them trust, 9.152-198, 10.598-615); Kurumi (お嬢ちゃん, then much harder to hear once she questions what kind of man he is, 10.373-598); Mizuki (no response to her wink, 9.92-126). The closing section states that the evidence is strongest in these particular relationships: an old friend asking him to yield gets latitude, a stranger's accusation does not. Not A: one story, and neither his response to his daughter's use of his account nor any conversation with her about the day is given. Not C: each relationship has located acts and a stated difference.

The story is told largely from others' viewpoints. Located avowals: wanting to be himself (9.210-243); trusting Mika, so he saw no need for a watcher (10.323-340); anyone accused of trying to kill his daughter would give off menace (10.575-598); finding the children remarkable. The portrait leaves open his motive for the invented lead time and whether he would only have looked at the computer. Not C: the two motives that matter most are left open, and his bereavement is not recounted. Not E: his avowals are located.

Located modes with outcomes: answering Chisato's challenge himself with defiance (9.210-243); silence at Kurumi's request to keep others out of the price of his self-image (9.243); a rapid reach toward Kurumi under accusation, restraint by Mika, a narrower account of his purpose, a concession that his anger was perceptible, and a dry laugh (10.575-598); dissatisfaction at being told to wait, then accepting Mika's appeal to trust (10.598-615). Not B: each mode occurs once and the prose leaves his intent toward Kurumi open. Not D: the modes are distinct and located with outcomes.

The row does not claim ethics. Located only as a principle of defiance framed as self-image (9.210-243), and Kurumi's objection that others pay its price, which he does not answer. Not D: no weighing is shown.

Located: the coffee joke that restores ease with Mika (9.108-129); laughing at the Mustang's upkeep bill; laughing from the floor and praising the girls' technique (9.173-198); a wry smile at Mika's compliment about his child; a show of still being able to do something impressive (10.598-615). Not C: the portrait does not analyze his play beyond ease with an old friend and good humor at losing his dignity. Not E: several instances are located.

His appearance is confined to this story, and the portrait locates every claim it relies on by spine item and paragraph, keeping others' readings attributed: Mika's account of the booking against his own, Mizuki's reading of his glance, Kurumi's inference from the account. Not A: the row curates only this derived item, and the evidence is written register only. Not C: his whole appearance is covered with locators.

Located bounds against overreading: his declaration of principle is poor evidence that he would choose a contract over a daughter he believed in danger, since he knew the message came from her computer (9.641-653); he put no watcher on anyone (10.323-340); the advance came from his account, but neither transfer shows him authorizing the attack or settling the cancellation (10.373-795); his reach is not established as an attack, and the prose leaves open whether he would only have looked (10.575-598); the book identifies his claim of advance preparation as false (10.933-951); no new rule or permanent change follows; Mizuki's reading of his glance is hers; the addressee of his call is withheld and is not recovered from the later outing. Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

One day, ordered by spine item and paragraph, with a ten-year gap since he and Mika last met. Not B: there is no calendar date, and Mika's and Hikaru's accounts of when the park was booked differ, with the book siding with Mika. Not D: the within-day order is precisely located.

conditions: Illustrative written Japanese only, never quotation, in the located forms: familiar, honorific-free address and teasing appraisal with Mika; 娘を頼むよ and お嬢さん方 to the young women; お嬢ちゃん to Kurumi; 俺 where someone tells him how a man should act; terse questions under urgency (9.108-243, 10.371-613).
Interlocutors are the sampled ones: Mika, Clarisse, Chisato, Takina, Kurumi and Mizuki.
Excluded: performed voice or timing, business negotiation, and any conversation with Clarisse about the hired pair or when he understood what she needed.
scenario_readiness.note: The row claims speech in written register only. The located forms constrain illustrative written lines with the sampled interlocutors.

conditions: A problem he understands and can pay to solve: predict energetic action and a finished solution presented to the beneficiary, possibly with a story about how it came about (9.98-115, 9.283-304, 10.933-951).
An open threat, or someone telling him how a man ought to act: predict defiance framed as being himself (9.210-243).
An old friend asks him to yield the immediate decision: predict visible dissatisfaction, then latitude and trust (10.598-615).

A stranger's accusation touching his daughter: predict a quick, physically assertive response whose look from the other side he misses, a narrower account of his purpose afterward, and a concession when a friend challenges him (10.575-598). Do not predict assault: his intent is left open.
Skill or perception from young people: predict credit and praise, even at the cost of his dignity (9.152-198).
Include his mistakes: treating a diagnosed cause as the end of the danger, arranging a scene to produce a reaction, claiming more foresight than he had, and frightening someone with less power.

Exclude a choice between a deal and a daughter he believes is truly in danger, any conversation with Clarisse about the day, his business negotiations and employees, romance, and anything after the story.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The one day of Gluttony days' first story, with his history (the friendship with Mika, his business abroad, his wife's death) as background. Nothing after the story.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Mika as an old friend of ten years' absence; Clarisse as his daughter; Chisato and Takina as young professionals he engages; Kurumi as an accuser; Mizuki as café staff. A comparable new old friend or new accuser is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: A business visit to Tokyo, Café LycoReco and the places of the story, with his wealth available.
No television identity, no setting in the regions where he works, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's closing expectation and the located acts behind it. The motive that would decide a real conflict between work and his daughter is not established, so that conflict is excluded.

conditions: Café and family settings as located: an old friend's counter, the coffee joke, the Mustang, film references, care for a carsick daughter (9.98-198).
Excluded: daily life in South America or the Middle East, his household routine, and his conduct as a partner.
scenario_readiness.note: The café visit and his tastes are well located; his life abroad is not.
No weighing is shown, the row does not claim ethics, and his located principle is a self-image that he does not defend against Kurumi's objection.
The portrait calls his romantic life after his wife's death opaque and attributes the reading of his glance to Mizuki.

His business is described, not shown: the negotiations happen offstage, his old work with Mika is unspecified, and his temperament with employees is unknown. Engaging the café staff is covered under cross-scenario conditions.

known_limits.statement: His declaration of principle is poor evidence that he would choose a contract over a daughter he believed in danger: he knew the threat was her own contrivance, and the portrait says the evidence is much weaker for any claim that he will always choose business first (9.210-243, 9.641-653).
The prose leaves open whether he would only have looked at the computer; he gives no apology to Kurumi, and no attack is established (10.575-625).
His claim of advance preparation for the park is false, and the portrait leaves open whether he meant to spare Clarisse or himself; no new rule, conversation or permanent change follows (10.933-951).
The advance from his personal account does not show him authorizing the attack, and the second transfer is Clarisse's report; his response to her use of the account is not given (10.373-795).
His portrait is confined to one story and to written register; the novel offers no performed accent or vocal timing.
His bereavement, romantic life, education, daily life where he works, old business with Mika and temperament with employees are unrecounted or opaque.
Untested: a real threat to Clarisse that forces a choice against an unsigned deal, a conversation with Clarisse about what happened, and his conduct with employees or business partners.
